role_policy.mechanism: v4.2 generalised the role filter from the v4.1 binary .role-full CSS class into a data-roles="a,b,c" attribute plus an allowed(el, role) function that hides any element whose data-roles list excludes the active role. Presentation-only, confirmed: no ACL or authority logic is attached; the footer text and each role's own workspaceDesc field state this explicitly.

steward.scope: all Contexts / Offerings; may focus many

role_policy.finding_for_steward_attention: The dispatched alignment brief's own instruction was explicit: 'Do not activate the Client role yet without Front Door release.' The live v4.2 Navigator's role selector already lists Client as a selectable option with a fully built ROLES entry and its own Flow-mode 'Assigned Flow surface' section -- i.e. Client is UI-present and selectable today, not merely designed. This may be intentional (a Front Door release may have already been granted between the brief's filing and v4.2's build) or it may be a live discrepancy against the brief's own instruction -- this candidate does not resolve which, only flags it plainly rather than silently accepting the more-permissive live state as correct.

known_gaps_disclosed: odoo_action_id values are read-only references copied from the live HTML at extraction time; this file does not verify they still resolve in Odoo and is not a live query.
agent_target fields are null throughout because no SynapSys Agent host adapter exists yet; they are placeholders for a future host, not a claim that one exists.

This registry does not include the six per-mode Odoo top-action shortcuts (Work Objects/Services/Benefits/Canonical Library) shown above the Flow-mode grid, since they duplicate action IDs already listed under flow_mode_routes and libraries above rather than adding new routes.

form_mode_routes and flow_mode_routes below have NOT been re-annotated with v4.2's new per-route data-roles restrictions (e.g. Canvas suite is architect-only, several Flow cards are architect/steward-only, Collaborator/Client see a role-filtered-pending placeholder section instead of the global Flow grid). The route targets themselves are unchanged from v4.1 to v4.2 and remain accurate; only the role-visibility layer on top of them is new and not yet mirrored into this file. Flagged rather than silently omitted.

The live Navigator advanced from v4.1 (state revision 152) to v4.2 (revision 153) in roughly the time between this candidate's first draft and this update -- direct, first-hand evidence that a routes-manifest file maintained by hand will fall behind a Navigator under this much active concurrent development. This is the strongest argument yet for the freshness/last-read stamping layer (see freshness.py) applying to this file's own targets too, not just to the six external sources it references.
